input_rows: canonical eligible rows validating memory_row.schema.json, ordered by kind ASCII bytes then semantic_hash ASCII bytes

missing_index.QUESTION_RECOGNITION: emit one separate view instance for every index in legal_question_missing_indices[kind], in ascending integer order

exact_byte_construction.query_object: {fields: row.fields with exactly missing_index replaced by null, kind: row.kind, view: view_id}

boundaries.cue_end: immediately after the final ASCII ':' in ASCII('\nA:')
boundaries.completion_end: the LF following the JCS answer_object
boundaries.online_view: QUESTION_RECOGNITION at the query's sole null index; every schema-legal thinker query therefore has one registered cue

round_trip.decoder: select the view from the first two cue bytes; parse the remaining cue prefix through ASCII('\nA:') as exactly one JCS query_object; parse completion after its one leading space and before its one terminal LF as exactly one JCS answer_object; replace the sole null field with answer_object.value
round_trip.acceptance: decoded kind and fields must byte-equal the source semantic row and recomputed semantic_hash must equal row.semantic_hash
round_trip.failure: generic tokenizer/compiler fixture failure is INVALID_PRECONDITION before DEV; a realized heldout-row failure is INVALID_PRECONDITION after M1_OWN seals and before either fit; no repair, normalization, alternate template, or dropped view

touches.touch_definition: one touch is one presentation of the complete cue||completion||EOS training sequence; cue tokens after sequence position zero are supervised, so touches are neither answer-only exposures nor equalized optimizer mass
touches.scope: repetitions apply to LoRA full-sequence examples only; text readers expose one semantic read result per query and receive no touches
